title: "Nonlinear Least Squares Fitting"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

## Overview

This example demonstrates nonlinear least squares data fitting with an analytic Jacobian and Hessian using the `aoclda` package.

```{r library}
library(aoclda)
```

## Define Residual, Jacobian, and Hessian

```{r functions}
res_fun <- function(x, data) {
    t <- data$t
    y <- data$y
    x1 <- x[1]
    x2 <- x[2]
    return(x1 * exp(x2 * t) - y)
}

jac_fun <- function(x, data) {
    t <- data$t
    x1 <- x[1]
    x2 <- x[2]
    cbind(exp(x2 * t), t * x1 * exp(x2 * t))
}

hes_fun <- function(x, wr, data) {
    t <- data$t
    x1 <- x[1]
    x2 <- x[2]
    H <- matrix(0, 2, 2)
    v <- t * exp(x2 * t)
    H[2, 1] <- sum(wr * v)
    H[1, 2] <- H[2, 1]
    H[2, 2] <- sum(wr * (t * x1) * v)
    H
}
```

## Data and Parameters

```{r data}
t <- c(1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 5.0, 8.0)
y <- c(3.0, 4.0, 6.0, 11.0, 20.0)

n_coef <- 2
n_res <- 5
x0 <- c(2.5, 0.25)
w <- 0.12 * rep(1, 5)
blx <- c(0.0, 0.0)
bux <- c(5.0, 3.0)
```

## Fit

```{r fit}
ndf <- nlls$new(n_coef, n_res,
    weights = w,
    lower_bounds = blx,
    upper_bounds = bux,
    check_derivatives = "yes",
    verbose = 3L
)

x_fitted <- ndf$fit(x0,
    fun = res_fun,
    jac = jac_fun,
    hes = hes_fun,
    data = list(t = t, y = y),
    abs_gtol = 1e-7, gtol = 1e-9,
    fd_ttol = 1.1e-4, fd_step = 1e-5,
    maxit = 20L
)
```

## Results

```{r results}
cat(sprintf("Solution found in %d iterations\n", ndf$n_iter))
cat(sprintf("Residual norm at solution: %.4f\n", ndf$metrics$obj))
cat(sprintf("x[0] = %.5f  (expected: 2.54105)\n", ndf$coef[1]))
cat(sprintf("x[1] = %.5f  (expected: 0.25950)\n", ndf$coef[2]))
```
